_comment: Protected paths for the agent layer (Phase 4). A PR touching any of these fails the required `path-guard` check, gets a comment naming the path, and is labeled needs-input. Agents propose changes to these via issue, never make them. Matching is done by .github/scripts/path-guard.sh with bash pattern syntax as used by `[[ $file == $glob ]]` — `*` and `**` both span `/` — and BOTH the new and the previous filename of a rename are matched, so a protected file cannot be moved out of its directory to escape. Three groups: (1) the agent's own instructions and prompt templates, (2) the local-safety enforcement layer — the harness settings, the git/Claude hooks, the test preload and the pipeline/gate shell scripts that keep agents off production data, since a PR that edits its own guard is a PR that has no guard, (3) the production publishing path and the launchd plists. package.json, tsconfig.json and bun.lock are listed because package.json defines the build, typecheck and deploy entry points that the pipeline and the required ci check run (a PR could otherwise set typecheck to a no-op); scripts/redeploy.sh and scripts/phase3-weekly.sh are publishing paths beside daily-automated.sh. src/config/active-source-ids.ts is listed because it defines the population the yield canary monitors: dropping a source from it silences the canary for that source, which is a human decision. Deliberately NOT protected (the Sunday retro PR edits them): .claude/notes/**, .claude/analyst-playbook.md, exemplars/**. No root CLAUDE.md exists today; the project file is .claude/CLAUDE.md — both are listed so a future root file is covered too. No enrichment prompt-template directory exists; the docs that function as enrichment prompt templates are listed individually. Added in the security loop (round 1): .claude/commands/**, .claude/skills/** and .claude/agents/** are agent instructions that sessions load and follow, like the files in group (1); netlify/** is code deployed to production with the site (group 3); docker/** is protected ahead of first use because a container definition sets what an agent run can reach; SECURITY.md is the disclosure channel — a PR that redirects it would route vulnerability reports to someone else; .github/CODEOWNERS is listed by name although .github/** covers it, so narrowing that glob later cannot drop it; and the security tests (tests/db-guard-hook.test.ts, tests/settings-security-pins.test.ts, tests/path-guard.test.ts, tests/netlify-headers.test.ts, tests/workflow-security.test.ts, scripts/__tests__/deploy-gate.test.ts) are listed because a PR that weakens a guard could otherwise delete the matching test in the same diff and keep ci green. scripts/db-read.ts is the only database access the enrichment session is granted, so it is part of the guard layer (group 2); tests/db-read.test.ts, tests/auto-enrich-guard-selftest.test.ts, tests/docker-hardening.test.ts and tests/security/** are its and the output-safety guards' tests. Added in the security loop (round 2): the enrichment chain the unattended session is allowed to run (scripts/save-batch.ts, write-description.ts, write-tags.ts, auto-gate-check.ts), the brief that frames scraped text as untrusted data (scripts/generate-enrichment-brief.ts), and the modules those scripts and the publishing path rely on for containment and URL safety (src/utils/batch-output-path.ts, outbound-url.ts, safe-url.ts, src/ingest/allowed-senders.ts, src/validators/published-artifacts.ts, scripts/lib/chrome-path.ts; some exist only on the regular branch and are listed ahead of the merge), plus the round-2 guard tests. .github/scripts/trusted-issue-thread.sh and .github/audit-ignore.json sit under .github/**.
